provenance.note: Authored fictional educational design briefs and chapter narratives; no commercial product specifications, measured deployment claims, or autonomous driving approval.
provenance.coverage: All episodes 0–16 specify intended investigations. Existing numerical studies are separately versioned generic mechanism fixtures; task-matched project support and release evidence remain to be implemented and reviewed.

scenarios.title: The activity ring
scenarios.mission: Develop a fictional wellness ring that recognizes everyday activities from sensor windows and produces useful personal activity summaries. Carry one deployment case from an unproven baseline to a bounded release decision.
scenarios.stakeholder: A wearer wants useful summaries without constantly charging, managing connections, or correcting confidently wrong activity labels. The product team must explain what the ring can support.
scenarios.workload: A versioned stream of sampled motion-sensor windows, transformed into features or tensors and classified on the ring. Window shape, observation schedule, activity labels, and operating conditions are explicit scenario inputs rather than inferred product specifications.
scenarios.boundary: Sensing, buffering, preprocessing, deployed inference, and summary handoff are in scope. Training and adaptation run on a separately identified development host. A companion phone or remote service is an alternative investigated at a named boundary, not an assumed always-available dependency.
success: Useful activity evidence for the declared wear conditions plus feasible working memory, package storage, response, mission energy, and sustained operation. Retaining a simpler baseline, restricting supported use, or holding release can be defensible outcomes.
unknowns: Which activities and wear conditions are supported by independent labeled evidence?
Does the evaluated package run with the declared preprocessing and runtime on the endpoint?
What are the complete sensing, inference, transfer, and background energy costs?
What changes when wear behavior or sensor processing changes?
No medical diagnosis, treatment, or commercial-ring specification claim.
No training a substantial model on an MCU by implication.
No sleep, heart-rate, or clinical inference is added to a motion-activity task without a separately specified sensor, task, and evidence contract.

acts.title: Earn a reason to build
acts.arc: Distinguish useful activity behavior from a running executable, locate the computation, and establish lifecycle and data contracts.

acts.title: Develop the ring candidate
acts.arc: Expose state and architecture costs, choose execution policies, and train a traceable candidate on a separate development host.

acts.title: Earn the endpoint claim
acts.arc: Preserve difficult activities in selection, convert and map the package, and challenge the actual ring benchmark.

acts.title: Operate and defend the ring
acts.arc: Schedule useful observations, recover processing incidents, audit supported use and lifecycle costs, and make a coherent release decision.

episodes.title: Join the ring team
episodes.question: What are we building, and how will we investigate it?
episodes.scene: A product brief asks for personal activity summaries from a ring that is worn during ordinary life. No architecture has been approved.
episodes.choice: Choose the ring mission; distinguish the ring from its development host and any optional companion path.
episodes.consequence: Choosing a mission fixes the story and vocabulary. It does not establish feasibility or approve a model.
episodes.task: Rehearse a supplied comparison: predict, change one control, pin evidence, distinguish live from captured state, and restore or download the record.
episodes.handoff: Mission card, intended-use boundary, and a clearly labeled rehearsal record; the first chapter starts with an unproven baseline.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: It runs, but is it useful?
episodes.question: Should the team change data, the model, or the machine first?
episodes.scene: The baseline executes successfully, yet supplied labeled outcomes show poorer activity summaries under a changed wear condition.
episodes.choice: Choose an evidence-supported first intervention instead of automatically asking for a faster processor.
episodes.consequence: Healthy execution cannot establish useful behavior; a promising quality change can still fail a separate resource gate.
episodes.task: Compare healthy runtime with activity outcomes; decompose execution time; try an intervention that leaves the binding term untouched; contrast data, algorithm, and machine efficiency levers.
episodes.handoff: Named baseline, intended-use statement, outcome limitation, full execution breakdown, and first action or hold.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Where should activity recognition happen?
episodes.question: Can moving work off the ring repair the actual constraint?
episodes.scene: A teammate proposes transmitting sensor windows to a companion path because its processor is faster.
episodes.choice: Compare ring-local, raw-transfer, and local-filter-plus-remote alternatives under the same useful activity task.
episodes.consequence: Faster remote arithmetic cannot erase a disqualifying trip; less observation can save energy while defeating the feature; a partition creates a versioned interface obligation.
episodes.task: Find a locality exclusion; repair SRAM and flash constraints separately; locate any observation-preserving energy and power region; screen feasibility before comparing supported costs.
episodes.handoff: Conditional placement decision with workload and connection assumptions, separate resource gates, rejected remedy, and unresolved complete-path obligations.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: A requirement changes
episodes.question: Which earlier decisions must reopen?
episodes.scene: The intended activity vocabulary now requires temporal context that the current window contract does not preserve.
episodes.choice: Trace which requirements, collected windows, model inputs, package, and validation records depend on the old contract.
episodes.consequence: Changing a requirement does not invalidate everything, but a model evaluated on the old input meaning cannot inherit a new release pass.
episodes.task: Frame improvement against the baseline; trace revise, retrain, and retest dependencies; allocate the next development window; distinguish a repaired artifact from a validated release.
episodes.handoff: Versioned requirement and dependency map, retained evidence, targeted repair plan, and explicit release hold where evidence is missing.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Build evidence we can trust
episodes.question: Are activity labels and preprocessing describing the same task on the host and ring?
episodes.scene: Overlapping windows from the same wearing session reach both training and test, while a ring preprocessing update uses different fitted normalization state.
episodes.choice: Choose session/person separation, an activity-label rubric, and a persisted train-fitted transformation bundle.
episodes.consequence: An impressive leaked score and identical preprocessing source code can coexist with untrustworthy evaluation or mismatched runtime features.
episodes.task: Compare label adjudication with coverage; inspect grouping and fit scope separately; repair keyed host/ring parity; find the input-feed bottleneck; distinguish a distribution alert from labeled evidence of damage.
episodes.handoff: Immutable source, split, label, and transformation identities; data audit; delivery limit; unresolved population evidence.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: The weight file is not the whole model
episodes.question: What state does this candidate require in each execution phase?
episodes.scene: A wider activity classifier looks small enough when the team checks only its stored weights.
episodes.choice: Change supported layer or window shapes while preserving input and output meanings; separate endpoint inference from host training.
episodes.consequence: Wider layers increase work and state differently from deeper layers; training retains gradients, optimizer state, and activations the ring does not need.
episodes.task: Inspect layer contributions, nonlinearity, backward operands, and phase-specific memory; contrast host batch reuse with retained activation growth without pretending it is a ring request scheduler.
episodes.handoff: Candidate topology and input shape plus separate ring-inference and development-host state inventories.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Preserve the motion pattern
episodes.question: Which architecture matches the activity evidence and the endpoint?
episodes.scene: Some activities have similar aggregate motion but different temporal order; extending context changes the candidate cost signature.
episodes.choice: Compare supported temporal convolution, recurrence, and attention candidates on the same specified activity task.
episodes.consequence: Discarding temporal information can make a cheap representation unsuitable; recurrence, attention, and convolution impose different dependencies and state.
episodes.task: Probe the information each family retains; inspect operator and resource signatures as context grows; separate attention score work from optional materialization. Use explicitly separate language and embedding reference cases for decode/KV and high-cardinality capacity concepts.
episodes.handoff: Matched-task architecture shortlist, context envelope, supplied quality evidence, and explicit target-device validation gap; reference-case observations remain separately scoped.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: From development graph to ring executable
episodes.question: When do execution optimizations repay their setup cost?
episodes.scene: The host frequently changes experiments, while the ring repeatedly executes a mostly fixed inference graph.
episodes.choice: Choose execution and compilation policies separately for the development workload and endpoint reuse pattern.
episodes.consequence: Compilation can lose on changing signatures, and fusion cannot discard a value needed by the backward pass; framework changes do not alter the task's mathematical operation count.
episodes.task: Expose graph breaks and dispatch overhead; compare visible fusion with held arithmetic; charge compilation across actual reuse; inspect retained differentiation state on the host.
episodes.handoff: Execution-plan record naming location, signatures, setup cost, steady work, reuse condition, and runtime/package dependencies.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Produce a trainable candidate
episodes.question: Which recipe reaches the same activity-quality target within the development allowance?
episodes.scene: The chosen model exceeds a development-host memory reservation; a faster-looking recipe also changes numerical behavior.
episodes.choice: Compare memory interventions, precision, batch or accumulation, checkpointing, and adaptation scope using compatible supplied learning evidence.
episodes.consequence: A cheaper step or larger nominal batch is not proof of less time to useful quality, and training success does not qualify the converted ring artifact.
episodes.task: Inventory all training state; recover an out-of-memory run; compare observed target-reaching time and failure cases; diagnose stalled quality before spending more compute.
episodes.handoff: Traceable host training recipe, data/model identity, convergence evidence or failure, and a separate conversion-and-device-validation requirement.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.
core_concepts: Profile to find the binding term

episodes.title: Keep the difficult windows
episodes.question: Does data selection reduce total development work without erasing important activity conditions?
episodes.scene: Repeated easy windows dominate collection, while unusual activity transitions and wear conditions are sparse.
episodes.choice: Choose a selection policy against the full-data baseline while preserving declared coverage obligations.
episodes.consequence: Aggressive removal can save steps yet lose the very conditions the ring must recognize; scoring and retrieval can consume the apparent saving.
episodes.task: Compare marginal learning value, rare-condition coverage, selection preparation, and actual data-path delivery at matched target quality.
episodes.handoff: Selected-data manifest, retained coverage and quality evidence, complete preparation/path cost, and a rejected policy.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.
core_concepts: Selection engineering on the data path

episodes.title: Make a deployable package
episodes.question: Which compression repairs the binding limit without losing the supported task?
episodes.scene: The development checkpoint is promising, but its converted package or working state fails a ring resource reservation.
episodes.choice: Choose among supported quantized, pruned, or distilled deployment artifacts using measured or authored matched-task evidence.
episodes.consequence: Fewer file bytes do not guarantee working-memory fit, supported kernels, faster execution, or preserved calibration and rare-condition quality.
episodes.task: Compare the quality/resource frontier; try an ineffective compression remedy; inspect dense/sparse and precision support; compare the actual combined artifact rather than multiplying separate speedups.
episodes.handoff: Identified deployment artifact and runtime, calibration evidence, repaired and unresolved gates, and a rejected alternative.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Feed the computation
episodes.question: Would a different mapping or faster execution unit improve the actual ring feature?
episodes.scene: An upgrade proposal advertises more arithmetic, but the candidate may be limited by operand movement or an unsupported primitive.
episodes.choice: Choose a legal supported mapping or machine change at an explicitly named endpoint or development-host boundary.
episodes.consequence: A larger peak helps only the relevant bound; illegal tiles do not execute, and unchanged sensing or preprocessing can dominate the application.
episodes.task: Inspect roofline ceilings, operand supply, retained-operand traffic and movement energy; cross a tile capacity or fringe boundary; carry a legal local improvement into the complete path.
episodes.handoff: Mapping and machine recommendation with legality, resource assumptions, traffic consequences, and application-level limitation.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Challenge the desk-test claim
episodes.question: What can the team honestly claim about the deployed ring?
episodes.scene: A favorable warm inference measurement becomes a proposed claim about everyday activity recognition.
episodes.choice: Specify the claim boundary and a repeatable protocol before accepting a speed or quality statement.
episodes.consequence: Kernel timing omits sensing and preprocessing; a mean hides slow observations; aggregate accuracy can conceal poorly supported wear conditions.
episodes.task: Compare micro, model, and full-path boundaries; allocate independent repeats; challenge operating-condition representativeness; inspect calibration, critical slices, and uncertainty.
episodes.handoff: Bounded benchmark claim with artifact, protocol, conditions, population, uncertainty, and explicit untested behavior.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Serve observations without hiding gaps
episodes.question: Which scheduling policy keeps activity summaries useful when observation work arrives unevenly?
episodes.scene: The chosen observation cadence competes for finite buffers and execution time; accumulating windows can improve reuse but delay or drop useful observations.
episodes.choice: Compare immediate dispatch, bounded grouping, and admission or reduced-service policies for the same input trace.
episodes.consequence: Work saved is not waiting removed; discarding windows can protect latency while weakening observation coverage and the user's summary.
episodes.task: Budget the complete observation path; measure backlog, headroom, formation delay, state, and lost service. Keep language streaming/KV experiments as named reference contrasts, never as ring cache evidence.
episodes.handoff: Observation-serving policy with demand envelope, buffer limits, retained versus lost service, and a trigger for changing the schedule.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Recover from a processing incident
episodes.question: Can the team identify and undo the release that changed activity decisions?
episodes.scene: After an update, feature values change for recorded windows while runtime health remains normal; outcome labels arrive later.
episodes.choice: Choose an evidence-timed response and restore a compatible preprocessing/model/runtime bundle.
episodes.consequence: A distribution alert does not identify the defect; reverting weights alone can leave changed normalization or cached state in place. Shadow or standby copies consume real capacity.
episodes.task: Route early alerts to an owner; replay request-keyed transformations; recover immutable lineage; budget any second resident copy or choose a feasible alternative; test rollback of the actual incident.
episodes.handoff: Incident record, monitored indicators, exact release bundle, capacity-feasible rollout/recovery plan, and tested response.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Useful for whom, at what cost?
episodes.question: Does the activity proxy serve the intended wearer across supported conditions?
episodes.scene: The team considers optimizing a convenient activity-score proxy, while correction feedback is available mostly for predictions users choose to review.
episodes.choice: Choose justified supplied population obligations, a permitted mitigation, an independent audit policy, and a matched lifecycle comparison.
episodes.consequence: Optimizing the proxy can miss the wellness-summary goal; selectively observed corrections can reinforce errors; reduced inference energy alone does not establish lower lifecycle emissions.
episodes.task: Compare proxy and goal evidence, subgroup pass/fail/insufficient states, mitigation trade-offs, censored-label feedback, and equal-service lifecycle cost and energy/carbon boundaries.
episodes.handoff: Intended-use restrictions, supported populations, audit and mitigation obligations, complete declared cost boundary, and unresolved responsibility gates.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Defend the ring release
episodes.question: Which single configuration does the accumulated evidence actually support?
episodes.scene: The release review contains attractive results from different windows, data versions, compressed artifacts, and operating conditions.
episodes.choice: Release a bounded configuration, restrict use, retain the simpler baseline, choose a supported fallback, or hold.
episodes.consequence: Incompatible green results cannot be assembled into a fictitious passing ring; a changed serving path can reopen both physical and behavioral claims.
episodes.task: Reconcile requirement/data/package/runtime/protocol identities; carry the selected improvement through the complete path; challenge its operating envelope; respond to a supplied change using prior concepts only.
episodes.handoff: A defensible deployment dossier with chosen and rejected options, compatible evidence, limits, owner, revisit trigger, and the next evidence request.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

scenarios.study_boundary: These fictional design briefs use generic illustrative fixtures only where explicitly identified; those studies do not validate the target deployment. Fictional educational narrative specification. Proposed project episodes do not imply implemented, task-matched numerical models or validated notebooks. Generic controlled mechanism studies remain separate from target-specific quality, performance, and release evidence. Training occurs on a named development host, not implicitly on the deployed endpoint.
scenarios.storyline:
The ring begins as a convincing activity demonstration, then fails under a changed wearing condition. The first response is to ask what the failure means, rather than move the same problem to a faster companion processor. The team makes its activity and temporal-context requirements explicit, discovers that overlapping sessions and inconsistent normalization undermine its evidence, and rebuilds the data contract.

The middle of the story is the effort to preserve useful temporal information on a tiny endpoint. Wider models and longer windows create state the weight file did not reveal. The team develops and trains on a separate host, compares supported structures and execution plans, and asks whether rare activity transitions justify their preparation cost. Compression and mapping must preserve the exact task rather than merely produce a small file.

The final act tests the difference between an inference that runs and a ring service that remains useful. Observation cadence competes with energy and buffering. A healthy-looking feature update changes outputs; selective corrections leave important outcomes unseen. At the final review, students defend a specific sensing, preprocessing, model, runtime, and observation bundle for declared wear conditions, or explain why the evidence supports only restriction or hold.

scenarios.title: The on-device photo organizer
scenarios.mission: Build a phone feature that assigns useful visual categories to a user's photos so they can browse and retrieve them locally. Follow one app feature from a rough baseline to an evidence-supported release.
scenarios.stakeholder: A phone owner wants to find photos and correct categories without disruptive foreground delays, battery drain, unwanted uploads, or an app that crowds out other tasks.
scenarios.workload: New-photo ingestion and bounded background indexing produce local category metadata; foreground browsing or retrieval reads that metadata. Image decode, resizing, model inference, metadata writes, device state, and interaction traces are explicit parts of the scenario.
scenarios.boundary: One application sharing a handheld device with other applications and the user interface. Model development occurs on a separate host. An optional remote recognition path is compared only when user policy and the modeled connection allow it; it is not silently required for local browsing.
success: Useful category and retrieval outcomes under declared photo conditions, timely foreground interaction, feasible shared memory and sustained power, and a clear user-data policy. Background throughput is assessed alongside user-visible service.
unknowns: Which photo categories and capture conditions have sufficient outcome evidence?
Do decoding and normalization match between development and the installed app?
What happens to responsiveness and state when another app consumes resources?
Which local corrections are observed, and whose errors remain invisible?
No server fleet, multi-region architecture, or always-on remote assistant is implied.
Photo classification does not establish semantic language generation or KV-cache behavior.
No commercial phone hardware or battery figures are invented.

acts.title: Earn the phone claim

acts.title: Maintain useful interaction

episodes.title: Join the photo-organizer team
episodes.question: What experience should this phone feature provide?
episodes.scene: A user has a growing photo collection and wants useful local organization without surrendering control of uploads or waiting through indexing.
episodes.choice: Choose the mobile mission and identify the user interaction, app boundary, development host, and optional remote alternative.
episodes.consequence: A project choice establishes intended use; it does not prove that local inference or a particular model will work.
episodes.task: Rehearse prediction, a controlled change, pinning, saved versus live state, and record restoration or download.
episodes.handoff: Mission preference, user-visible goal, and a labeled rehearsal comparison; continue with an unproven local baseline.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: The app is healthy; the categories are not
episodes.question: What should change when users cannot find the photos they expect?
episodes.scene: The app opens normally, but supplied labeled personal-photo outcomes expose failures hidden by a favorable curated demonstration.
episodes.choice: Choose a data, algorithm, or machine investigation before accepting a hardware upgrade.
episodes.consequence: Faster indexing can still produce unhelpful categories; a better classifier may be unacceptable if the installed app violates its execution budget.
episodes.task: Compare outcome and runtime evidence; decompose decode, transfer, inference, and fixed work; try an intervention that leaves the binding term unchanged; contrast the three efficiency levers.
episodes.handoff: Baseline and intended-use statement, supported photo conditions, full execution breakdown, and an evidence-supported first action.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Keep recognition local or send photos?
episodes.question: Which placement respects both useful interaction and user policy?
episodes.scene: A remote recognition service promises more compute, but the app handles personal images over a variable connection and shares phone resources.
episodes.choice: Compare local recognition, raw upload, and a declared local-filter/remote path while holding the recognition task fixed.
episodes.consequence: The network trip can remain disqualifying despite fast remote inference; more battery does not remove sustained-power limits; filtered paths introduce new interfaces and quality obligations.
episodes.task: Find locality limits; distinguish package storage from working memory; test useful background activity against energy and sustained power; screen policy and feasibility before comparing matched costs.
episodes.handoff: Conditional placement and data-movement policy, resource gates, rejected workaround, and interface obligations.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: A local-use promise becomes a requirement
episodes.question: What must change when the feature must remain useful without a connection?
episodes.scene: A product review makes previously ambiguous offline behavior explicit for category browsing and new-photo processing.
episodes.choice: Trace which app states, fallback behavior, data contracts, candidate packages, and tests depended on remote availability.
episodes.consequence: A new requirement propagates through concrete artifacts; a download preference alone does not establish a working offline feature.
episodes.task: State measurable behavior relative to the baseline; map dependency rework; choose the next development action; distinguish repaired contracts from complete release evidence.
episodes.handoff: Versioned offline/connected behavior contract, dependency map, targeted repair and retest plan, and unresolved gates.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: A collection is not an independent test set
episodes.question: Are the labels, splits, and installed preprocessing trustworthy?
episodes.scene: Burst photos and edited copies cross the evaluation boundary, and the installed decoder/resize pipeline differs from development.
episodes.choice: Choose event or duplicate-group splits, a category-label rubric, and a persisted train-fitted transform bundle.
episodes.consequence: Near-duplicate leakage can flatter the score; legal tensors with different crop, orientation, or normalization semantics can silently change behavior.
episodes.task: Inspect label disagreement and gold checks; separate split grouping from fit scope; replay keyed transformation parity; expose decode/feeding bottlenecks; distinguish input alerts from quality loss.
episodes.handoff: Versioned image/label/split/transform contract, leakage and parity findings, input-delivery limit, and missing population evidence.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Resolution changes more than the input file
episodes.question: What state and work does the candidate require on the phone and host?
episodes.scene: The team raises image resolution and network width to distinguish visually similar categories; checking weight size misses intermediate state.
episodes.choice: Change supported shapes while preserving the classification task and separate inference buffers from training state.
episodes.consequence: Weight storage, peak activations, and host optimizer state answer different capacity questions; batching reuses weights while retaining more activations.
episodes.task: Inspect layer-level shape costs and nonlinear composition; identify backward operands; compare training and inference state; locate the batch reuse/capacity boundary on the named host.
episodes.handoff: Candidate shape contract and distinct phone-inference and host-training state budgets.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Choose a model for personal photos
episodes.question: Which architecture preserves the information this organizer needs?
episodes.scene: Tiny thumbnails make some categories indistinguishable, while a larger or patch-based candidate imposes different work and memory demands.
episodes.choice: Compare supported convolutional and attention-based image candidates on matched supplied photo evidence.
episodes.consequence: A cheap representation can discard relevant detail; attention cost depends on the image-token count and implementation; parameter count alone does not rank candidates.
episodes.task: Probe retained information; inspect architecture/operator signatures and resource interventions; separate attention work from score storage. Study autoregressive phases and embedding capacity on explicitly named reference tasks rather than relabeling image classification.
episodes.handoff: Matched-task architecture shortlist, resolution envelope, outcome support, and target-device validation requirement.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Stable photos, changing graphs
episodes.question: When should the app compile, fuse, or keep execution flexible?
episodes.scene: The app sees recurring processed image shapes but also occasional shape changes; development experiments still change frequently.
episodes.choice: Choose an execution policy using actual shape reuse and a separately identified development workload.
episodes.consequence: Compilation setup and graph breaks can consume a short session; fusion reduces dispatch/traffic only where visibility and saved-state requirements permit it.
episodes.task: Compare eager inspection with graph visibility; isolate launch overhead; charge compilation and signature reuse; inspect host differentiation state without claiming the phone trains the production model.
episodes.handoff: Execution-plan decision with signatures, location, setup/runtime separation, and reuse condition.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Train the organizer before shipping it
episodes.question: Which development recipe reaches useful photo quality?
episodes.scene: The development host runs out of memory on the chosen image/model shape, and a faster precision option changes the supplied learning trajectory.
episodes.choice: Compare memory repairs, numerical recipes, and adaptation scope on the same target and dataset identity.
episodes.consequence: Fast steps and high hardware occupancy do not establish fast arrival at useful quality; successful host training still needs app conversion and validation.
episodes.task: Account for all training state; recover a nonfitting run; compare target-reaching evidence across supported recipes; diagnose quality limitations before adding compute.
episodes.handoff: Training recipe and convergence evidence or explicit failure, with traceable data/model identity and separate installed-artifact qualification.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Do not delete the hard photos
episodes.question: Can selection save development work while preserving useful collection coverage?
episodes.scene: Bursts of easy scenes dominate the collection while low-light, unusual compositions, and less common categories are underrepresented.
episodes.choice: Choose deduplication or selection against a full-data baseline with fixed coverage obligations.
episodes.consequence: Removing redundancy may help, but filtering by apparent ease can erase valuable cases; scoring, reading, and materializing the subset may dominate.
episodes.task: Compare learning value, coverage, complete selection preparation, and delivered data-path savings at matched target quality.
episodes.handoff: Selected-data manifest, covered conditions, matched quality evidence, and complete preparation/path cost.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Fit the shared phone
episodes.question: Which deployment artifact repairs the actual installed-app limit?
episodes.scene: A promising candidate competes with the interface, decoded images, metadata, and other applications for working memory.
episodes.choice: Compare supported compressed packages under fixed app workload and quality gates rather than choosing the smallest file.
episodes.consequence: Storage savings do not guarantee reduced live state or supported acceleration; a sparse package can execute slowly and aggregate accuracy can hide damaged categories.
episodes.task: Explore the quality/resource frontier; try an ineffective size remedy; inspect calibration, supported precision, sparse/dense runtime, and an actual combined artifact.
episodes.handoff: Named app model package and runtime, quality evidence, repaired memory/storage/runtime gates, and remaining shared-device limitations.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Use the phone execution path that exists
episodes.question: Will acceleration improve the user-visible feature?
episodes.scene: The app can route supported operations to an accelerator, but some work falls back and image decode still occurs outside it.
episodes.choice: Choose supported execution units and legal mappings while retaining transfers, fallback operators, and unchanged app stages.
episodes.consequence: An advertised peak is irrelevant to unsupported work; operand supply and transfers can bind; a faster inference kernel may barely change a photo appearing in the organizer.
episodes.task: Inspect roofline and supply boundaries; compare dataflows and movement energy; cross tile capacity/fringe limits; carry the supported intervention through the complete feature path.
episodes.handoff: Mapping/runtime recommendation with legality, traffic, fallback accounting, and end-to-end consequence.
episodes.status: Narrative specification; matched project models and evidence require implementation review.

episodes.title: Benchmark the interaction, not the demo
episodes.question: What performance and quality claim survives a realistic phone protocol?
episodes.scene: A warm model-only measurement from an idle phone becomes a proposed claim that the organizer is responsive during everyday use.
episodes.choice: Define the timer boundary, shared-device conditions, request mix, quality floor, and repeat protocol before comparing candidates.
episodes.consequence: Foreground delay, cold starts, decode, contention, and sustained operation can overturn a microbenchmark ranking; aggregate quality cannot certify every photo condition.

scenarios.storyline:
The phone story begins with a curated photo demonstration that does not match the owner's actual collection. A remote service offers more compute, but personal images, variable connections, offline browsing, and shared device resources make placement a product decision. The team clarifies what must work offline, then discovers that duplicate photos and inconsistent decode/resize behavior weakened the evaluation.

The central development thread is a photo category distinction that needs more visual information. Higher resolution and a more capable model create decoded-image and intermediate state, not just larger weights. On a separate development host, the team compares supported candidates, runtime paths, training recipes, and selection policies while preserving low-light and less common photo conditions. The installed artifact must coexist with metadata, the interface, and other applications.

The final act begins when a large import arrives while the user opens the organizer. Fast background throughput can still leave browsing unresponsive, and a smaller batch can be preferable to an impressive accelerator number. An app update changes orientation or crop handling without crashing. User corrections reveal only part of the error population. The closing decision names the exact app/model/transform bundle, foreground/background policy, supported collection and shared-device conditions, and what remains unknown.

scenarios.title: The onboard road-object perception project
scenarios.mission: Develop and evaluate a vehicle-mounted perception system that detects and labels road objects from camera frames, then defend the conditions under which its outputs are useful to an engineering evaluation team.
scenarios.stakeholder: A vehicle perception engineer needs timely, interpretable detections; the evaluation lead needs evidence tied to road conditions, object groups, and the exact deployed package.
scenarios.workload: Camera frame → timestamped ingestion → decode and calibrated preprocessing → onboard detector → postprocessing → labeled road-object records. Development and training use a separate host. The evaluation logger retains permitted records for later analysis.
scenarios.boundary: One vehicle-local perception computer and its camera-to-output path. Cloud services may support offline development or permitted logging; they do not provide real-time steering. Planning, actuation, closed-loop driving performance, and top-level vehicle safety are outside the demonstrated boundary.
success: Useful object outputs for a stated evaluation envelope, supported by matched outcome evidence and complete-path timing, memory, sustained-power, data-handling, and recovery requirements. Passing perception checks does not prove safe autonomous driving.
unknowns: Road-condition and object-group quality require matched detections and annotations; generic classification scores cannot stand in for them.
Input synchronization, decoding, detector postprocessing, dropped-frame semantics, and supported execution paths need scenario-specific fixtures.
No timing, energy, or weather robustness claim is established by this narrative.

scenarios.storyline:
The vehicle team needs useful road-object outputs for a declared engineering evaluation. A smooth demonstration fails under a changed capture condition, and a larger remote model does not remove the need for timely onboard evidence. The requirement to include bicycles becomes the recurring change: it affects labels, drive-group splits, transformations, input detail, architecture, and every later claim about the candidate.

The build sequence follows the bicycle-capable package from a data contract to a legal onboard artifact. More image detail grows intermediate state; a fashionable backbone lacks matched outcome evidence; an export can reject a required operation. Training, selection, and compression must preserve difficult object and capture conditions. Hardware mapping then tests whether camera, decode, host work, or postprocessing prevents an isolated kernel gain from helping the complete perception path.

During operation, bursts create old-frame backlogs even when throughput looks healthy. Dropping frames or waiting for batches trades timeliness against lost observation. An update changes paired-frame outputs and requires recovery of the compatible camera-transform-runtime-model bundle. The final review is explicitly an engineering evaluation of perception evidence and its limits, not permission for autonomous driving. Students may recommend restricted evaluation, a baseline or fallback, or a hold.

scenarios.title: The product recommendation endpoint
scenarios.mission: Build and operate a traditional cloud ML recommendation endpoint that ranks eligible e-commerce products for a shopping session, including newly listed items with no interaction history.
scenarios.stakeholder: A merchandising lead wants useful product discovery; shoppers need relevant, available suggestions, sellers need declared exposure obligations, and application developers need a dependable ranking request contract.
scenarios.workload: Ranking request with permitted session context and candidate product IDs → ingress and validation → versioned feature and embedding lookup → GPU-host ranking model → eligibility filtering and ranked product response. Candidate generation is a declared upstream input, not an unmodeled claim of catalog-wide retrieval. Training and adaptation run on an explicitly identified development host; deployment concerns one ranking host and its complete request path.
scenarios.boundary: Traditional recommendation inference on one cloud endpoint. Include candidate and feature preparation, embedding residency and lookup traffic, CPU work, host-device transfer, GPU ranking, queues, filtering, and responses where relevant. Feature snapshots and upstream candidates have explicit contracts. Fleet scaling, distributed training, multi-region routing, and generative language behavior are outside this project.
success: Useful product discovery on the stated shopper/session and catalog population, with a versioned candidate/feature/ranking contract that covers new items, complete-path latency distribution, admitted demand, catalog freshness, resident/live-state limits, data handling, operating cost, and tested recovery requirements.
unknowns: Ranking relevance, new-item coverage, and declared seller-exposure obligations require matched recommendation and outcome evidence; image classification or language outcomes cannot be relabeled.
Candidate eligibility, missing-history fallback, feature/embedding freshness, feedback attribution, and arrival traces require matched endpoint fixtures.
No cost, tail-latency, demand capacity, commercial benefit, or emissions result is established merely by choosing a cloud host.
