episodes.handoff: Shape-described ranking candidate and separate endpoint/development state inventories, including embedding and feature ownership.
episodes.scene: The team estimates capacity from the ranking checkpoint while ignoring product embeddings, candidate features, and batch activations introduced by the new-item fallback.
episodes.choice: Choose a supported candidate/batch envelope, change binding capacity, or reject the incomplete estimate.
episodes.consequence: Batch reuse can improve while live state grows; the ranking model file is neither complete serving residency nor training memory.
core_concepts: Network as linear maps and nonlinearities
Training holds four kinds of state
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Match the architecture to recommendation evidence
episodes.question: Which ranking architecture fits the task, and where does its cost bind?
episodes.task: Compare task-matched ID-based, content-feature, and supported hybrid ranking candidates with supplied relevance and new-item evidence. Vary embedding vocabulary/width, candidate count, or supported attention extent; trace lowered matrix work, irregular lookup traffic, and embedding capacity. Use a separately named language reference for autoregressive decode and KV state.
episodes.handoff: Task-matched architecture and candidate/embedding envelope, cold-start limits, and explicit language-reference boundary.
episodes.scene: A larger product embedding table is proposed to help new items even though unseen IDs still have no learned history.
episodes.choice: Adopt an evidenced content-aware candidate, retain a simpler fallback, restrict support, or request matched quality evidence.
episodes.consequence: Embedding capacity is a native recommendation constraint, but a larger ID table does not teach unseen products useful representations. Attention cost and language decode are distinct mechanisms.
core_concepts: Inductive bias buys data and cost
Autoregressive decode and the KV cache
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Repay setup on the ranking path
episodes.question: When should the endpoint compile or fuse its ranking graph?
episodes.task: Compare dispatch and fusion at fixed ranking semantics, charge graph compilation over observed reuse and shape changes, trace saved state on the development host, and test lookup/scoring/filtering operator support with boundary costs preserved.
episodes.handoff: Execution plan with graph and feature identities, setup/runtime separation, reuse condition, and endpoint compatibility.
episodes.scene: Repeated ranking requests reuse an execution graph, but varying candidate counts and feature signatures trigger new compilation events.
episodes.choice: Compile reusable signatures, bound supported shapes, retain debugging boundaries or eager execution, permit accounted fallback, or hold.
episodes.consequence: A fast scoring kernel does not repay setup automatically; unsupported feature or lookup operations remain in the request.
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Train the cold-start candidate
episodes.question: Which development-host recipe reaches the same ranking target acceptably?
episodes.task: Compare full versus restricted adaptation of embeddings and ranking layers, static/activation fit, accumulation or recomputation, and supported numerical recipes. Reveal matched progress evidence, then test ineffective and targeted repairs on the separate development host.
episodes.handoff: Development recipe and observed matched target evidence, or explicit target failure/absence and next validation request.
episodes.scene: Training the content-aware ranker misses its update window despite high GPU busy time, while new-item outcomes remain a required target.
episodes.choice: Repair the binding state or stage, retain the stable recipe, request joint recipe evaluation, or hold.
episodes.consequence: Busy time is not useful-work utilization; faster steps need not reach the relevance or new-item target, and retraining latency constrains achievable freshness.
core_concepts: Profile to find the binding term
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Choose information, not only fewer interactions
episodes.question: Does a selected interaction pool save the complete campaign without losing coverage?
episodes.task: Use work-matched pilots, preserve supplied item/seller/session and new-item coverage floors, and inspect displaced records and negative-sampling assumptions. Charge selection scoring, feature preparation, refresh, and training; compare scattered reads with materialized subsets while keeping selected identities fixed.
episodes.handoff: Selected-data or full-pool policy with ranking/coverage evidence, feedback limits, and complete preparation/path accounting.
episodes.scene: Popular products dominate the training archive while new items, less-exposed sellers, and sparse sessions have little observed feedback.
episodes.choice: Pay for justified selection and coverage, retain the pool, request representative observations, or hold.
episodes.consequence: Fewer selected interactions can still require full archive scans or reinforce popularity bias; a language-token frontier is not a recommendation quality law.
core_concepts: Selection engineering on the data path
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Compress a usable ranking bundle
episodes.question: Which compression improves the endpoint constraint without losing the intended ranking behavior?
episodes.task: Compare supported quantized, pruned, and combined ranking artifacts using matched relevance and coverage outcomes, embedding/model storage, resident/live state, and runtime. Inspect quality cliffs and actual lookup/kernel format support.
episodes.handoff: Exact model/embedding/feature deployment bundle, rejected alternatives, matched resource/outcome evidence, and open gates.
episodes.scene: A smaller embedding and ranker bundle is proposed to reduce residency, but new-item fallback features and low-frequency product scores may be affected.
episodes.choice: Choose an executable evidenced artifact, retain the baseline, restrict support, or hold for ranking and new-item validation.
episodes.consequence: A smaller bundle and sparse zeros do not establish faster ranking; isolated gains do not multiply, and task quality must be rechecked after the combined change.
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Supply the ranker, not just more arithmetic
episodes.question: What should change when a faster accelerator barely improves the request?
episodes.task: Compare compute, bandwidth, and reuse interventions on relevant rooflines; trace embedding and dense operand traffic, stationary schedules, movement energy, legal tile buffers, and alignment. Preserve feature preparation, lookup, transfers, launches, and filtering in total request time.
episodes.handoff: Legal mapping or host recommendation with counted traffic and complete ranking-request consequences.
episodes.scene: Dense scoring accelerates, but feature gathering and embedding access dominate the recommendation response.
episodes.choice: Repair supply or mapping, target the newly dominant request stage, retain the host, or hold.
episodes.consequence: A dense-kernel peak does not describe irregular embedding lookup, and Amdahl limits follow the fraction actually changed.
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Benchmark the promised recommendation
episodes.question: Which speed and relevance claim survives a matched endpoint protocol?
episodes.task: Repair the claim with matched ranking bundle, candidate/session mix, feature freshness, cold/warm conditions, timer boundary, repetitions, uncertainty, tails, and new-item coverage. Distinguish bounds, replayed observations, and measured results; keep ranking relevance separate from downstream benefit claims.
episodes.handoff: Reproducible endpoint protocol, bounded speed/relevance claims, supported populations, and missing outcome validation.
episodes.scene: A warm fixed-candidate scoring result is presented as the response time and relevance shoppers will receive, including new products.
episodes.choice: Narrow the claim, repeat the full request benchmark, retain the baseline, or withhold unsupported benefit and latency claims.
episodes.consequence: Scoring throughput does not establish arrival-to-response tails, cold-start relevance, or useful discovery for unobserved sessions.
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Serve timely recommendations under arrivals
episodes.question: Which batching and admission policy supports the declared shopping traffic?
episodes.task: Compare identical arrival traces, complete latency stages, queueing headroom, supported candidate/batch envelopes, waiting, rejected work, and model/embedding/live state. Declare feature freshness separately from response time. Examine prefill/decode and KV concurrency only in a separately named generative reference task.
episodes.handoff: Single-endpoint serving policy with supported demand, freshness limits, lost-service counts, state budget, and reversal trigger.
episodes.scene: A promotion causes bursts of ranking requests while newly listed inventory must enter eligible candidates without waiting indefinitely for feature refresh.
episodes.choice: Bound admission, choose a supported batching delay and freshness policy, keep immediate dispatch, or hold when no policy meets the contract.
episodes.consequence: Dropped requests are lost service; stale recommendations can arrive quickly, shorter waits do not automatically save work, and embedding tables are not a KV cache.
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Recover a compatible recommendation bundle
episodes.question: Can the team detect and recover the release without mixing feature and model identities?
episodes.task: Replay the update incident; separate early feature/exposure signals from delayed attributed feedback, compare request-keyed parity, reserve complete candidate/baseline copies, and test recovery of compatible model, embedding, feature-schema/snapshot, eligibility, and runtime identities.
episodes.handoff: Versioned release bundle, freshness and outcome monitors with owners, tested rollback, exposure/residency accounting, and evidence limits.
episodes.scene: A canary stays operationally healthy but its feature/embedding refresh changes rankings on paired requests and suppresses newly listed products.
episodes.choice: Diagnose the responsible artifact, recover a complete compatible bundle, restrict exposure, or hold.
episodes.consequence: Small traffic exposure is not small resident memory; rolling back only the scoring weights cannot repair a mismatched embedding vocabulary or feature transform.
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Recommendation changes its own evidence
episodes.question: Does the service improve discovery responsibly, or merely reinforce what it already shows?
episodes.task: Contrast click proxies with supplied independent discovery outcomes. Inspect justified seller/item or affected-population obligations and insufficient slices; compare supported coverage/exposure mitigations, audit exposure-conditioned feedback, and account lifecycle cost, energy, and emissions at matched service.
episodes.handoff: Intended-use restrictions, justified outcome and exposure obligations, feedback audit policy, lifecycle boundary, and unresolved responsibility gates.
episodes.scene: Only displayed products can receive clicks, and a click-optimized update raises engagement while new items and some sellers lose exposure.
episodes.choice: Request representative audits, choose an evidenced mitigation, restrict use, retain the baseline, or hold unsupported benefit claims.
episodes.consequence: More clicks do not by themselves prove useful discovery; selective exposure can amplify a feedback loop, and cheaper service is not automatically lower carbon.
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

episodes.title: Defend one coherent recommendation release
episodes.question: What can this exact ranking endpoint promise now?
episodes.task: Reconcile discovery requirements, candidate and feedback identities, feature/embedding snapshots, trained ranker, compressed bundle, runtime, benchmark, freshness/serving policy, and rollback evidence. Reject incompatible records and identify the next decisive test.
episodes.handoff: Release, restricted-use, baseline, fallback, or hold memo with compatible evidence, owner, and revisit trigger.
episodes.scene: Merchandising asks whether the service can recommend the stated catalog, including newly listed products, for its declared shopper and demand envelope.
episodes.choice: Release only the supported recommendation scope, restrict cold-start use, retain a baseline/fallback, or hold.
episodes.consequence: The final decision synthesizes compatible evidence; it neither invents a composite pass nor turns one-host evidence into fleet readiness or guaranteed commercial benefit.
episodes.status: Authored narrative specification; task-matched numerical fixtures and notebook implementation require separate review.

scenarios.study_boundary: These fictional design briefs use generic illustrative fixtures only where explicitly identified; those studies do not validate the target deployment. Author specification pending matched MLSysIM scenario fixtures; episodes describe proposed investigations, not completed experiments. No target-specific release claim follows from generic mechanism studies. Existing classification, language, or unrelated deployment observations require explicit task matching before reuse. Old classification-service records retain their original identity and are not recommendation evidence.
scenarios.storyline:
The retailer's recommendation endpoint is fast and available, yet newly listed products receive little exposure because they have no interaction history. This cold-start problem stays with the class throughout the volume. Moving every stage to a GPU does not create missing behavioral evidence. The team must define how eligible new products enter the candidate set, how content features reach the ranker, and which claims feedback can support.

Development follows the content-aware ranking candidate. A later-purchase join leaks future information, and feature snapshots differ between training and requests. A larger embedding table cannot learn an unseen ID by itself. The team trains and evaluates supported content-aware or hybrid candidates, preserves new-item and less-exposed conditions during selection, and qualifies an exact model/embedding/feature bundle. Acceleration must account for lookup, feature preparation, transfer, dense scoring, eligibility, and filtering on one endpoint; this is not a fleet-scaling story.

A promotion then introduces bursty requests while catalog features must remain fresh. A healthy canary suppresses new items after an incompatible refresh; rollback must recover the complete bundle and its data contracts. Clicks are exposure-conditioned, so rising engagement cannot alone establish better product discovery or justified treatment of affected sellers. The final decision states which catalog, sessions, freshness, demand, and outcome obligations the endpoint supports, with compatible evidence or an explicit hold.

volume_storyboard.title: From a promising model to a defensible deployment
volume_storyboard.premise: You are the systems engineer on one product team. The product does not change each week; the evidence does. Each chapter introduces a request, failure, or uncertainty that makes the next design decision necessary. You investigate with a notebook and maintain a deployment dossier that records what the team can support, what it rejected, and what must be revisited.
volume_storyboard.opening: At the start, the team has a stakeholder and a plausible baseline, not a deployed success. By the end, it must defend one exact artifact under declared use, workload, resource, evidence, and responsibility conditions. There is no predetermined winning device, largest model, or release verdict.
volume_storyboard.ending: The final scene is a deployment review. A recommendation may be release, limited evaluation or use, retaining a baseline, an explicit fallback, or a hold. The achievement is a traceable argument tied to compatible observations and a clear next test. Operation can send the team back to any earlier chapter.

chapters.headline: Join a team before choosing a machine
chapters.opening: You have joined a team with a useful ML product in mind and no approved deployment design. Choose the activity ring, personal photo organizer, onboard road perception system, or cloud recommendation endpoint. You will remain with that project while each chapter introduces a new decision. Your job is to investigate the evidence and defend what the team can do next.
chapters.previous: Start with the mission brief. There are no validated project results yet. The endpoint and the development host are different roles, even when the supplied exercises run in one browser.
chapters.goal: Learn the instruments and choose a project; do not optimize a system or certify feasibility.

investigations.title: Meet the projects
investigations.question: What changes when the deployment category changes, and what remains the same learning question?
investigations.interaction: Compare two mission cards, identify their stakeholder and system boundary, then choose one project.
investigations.notice: Device categories are contexts with different obligations, not a ranking from weak to strong.

investigations.title: Rehearse an investigation
investigations.question: Which action changes the live result, and which preserves evidence?
investigations.interaction: Use labeled interface-practice cases: predict, change a case, pin a baseline, capture a contrast, and move the live control again.
investigations.notice: A prediction is not an observation; a capture does not follow later control changes.

investigations.title: Practice keeping work
investigations.question: What survives closing this page?
investigations.interaction: Try the implemented storage/readback path and download a rehearsal discussion; expose a storage failure and its fallback honestly.
investigations.notice: Session state, a stored record, and a downloaded file have different meanings. Do not promise resume until it exists.

investigations.title: Make the first handoff
investigations.question: What will an instructor receive?
investigations.interaction: Inspect a short discussion built from the actual rehearsal; distinguish the selected project, original prediction, saved comparison, and next question.
investigations.notice: The submission communicates an investigation, not a quiz score or a declaration that the project works.

chapters.turning_point: Switching a live case after capture changes the display but leaves the captured comparison intact. That is the evidence habit used throughout the series.
chapters.dossier_entry: Project passport: mission identity and version, stakeholder, task, endpoint/development-host boundary, and a successful setup rehearsal or explicit storage fallback.
chapters.transition: The team now knows how to investigate. It still needs to decide what useful behavior means and whether a faster machine would repair its first problem.
chapters.qmd_bridge: Before the chapter labs, choose a project and practice the notebook workflow. Orientation teaches prediction, comparison, captured evidence, and discussion submission. It establishes no technical feasibility claim.

chapters.headline: The system runs. Is it useful?
chapters.opening: The first demonstration looks healthy: the program runs and the machine responds. Then someone reports that the useful outcome has worsened. A teammate proposes buying a faster machine. Before approving it, the team needs to separate what the model does from how the machine executes it.
chapters.previous: Bring the project passport. Begin with a labeled supplied baseline, not an invented history of prior successful experiments.
chapters.goal: Choose the next data, algorithm, or machine intervention using separate evidence of behavior and execution.

investigations.title: Healthy runtime, changed behavior
investigations.question: Can the system become less useful while weights and execution remain unchanged?
investigations.interaction: Change the supplied operating-population mixture at fixed candidate and runtime; reveal labeled outcomes only when available.
investigations.notice: An input warning precedes confirmed outcome evidence. Healthy infrastructure cannot establish trustworthy behavior.

investigations.title: Improve the right part of time
investigations.question: Would faster arithmetic materially improve the complete path?
investigations.interaction: Compare one capability counterfactual at a time against the same decomposition of compute, movement, and overhead.
investigations.notice: A large local improvement can leave the dominant term untouched; the intervention has a scope and an unpriced cost if no cost evidence is supplied.

investigations.title: Meet both requirements
investigations.question: Is the best-quality candidate deployable?
investigations.interaction: Compare task-matched candidates against distinct quality, latency, memory, and energy gates; retain failed and unknown candidates visibly.
investigations.notice: Averages or combined scores cannot compensate for a failed requirement.

investigations.title: Name the lever
investigations.question: Which part of the training task would this intervention change?
investigations.interaction: On the separate development host, compare supported changes in samples, work per sample, and realized time per operation while retaining the quality obligation.
investigations.notice: Different routes to efficiency have different evidence requirements. Fewer samples do not establish equal quality.

chapters.turning_point: The faster machine can improve execution while leaving the observed behavior problem unresolved. The high-quality model can also fail the deployment budget.
chapters.dossier_entry: An initial recommendation: first intervention or hold, chosen and rejected candidate, separate behavioral and execution evidence, and the observation that would reverse the decision.
chapters.transition: Once the team knows which constraint matters, it can ask where the pipeline should run. The next lab changes placement, not the definition of success.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter distinguishes useful learned behavior from feasible execution. In the lab, diagnose a changed outcome and test whether a data, algorithm, or machine intervention addresses it. Submit the evidence behind your first recommendation.

chapters.headline: Where should the work live?
chapters.opening: The team has a candidate and a proposed remedy. Someone suggests moving work to a faster processor. The proposal sounds simple until the input must travel, state must fit, and the service must remain useful when a connection or permission changes.
chapters.previous: Bring the task and separate outcome/execution requirements. Use compatible prior evidence when supported, or a clearly labeled supplied starting case.
chapters.goal: Defend a conditional placement or an explicit hold by screening locality, capacity, operation, and partition obligations.

investigations.title: Find the locality boundary
investigations.question: Can faster computation remove the transfer or propagation term that limits this path?
investigations.interaction: Choose a supported payload, link, or host/device-transfer contrast. Compare the complete declared path with an ideal-processor bound; do not add WAN propagation to a same-host link.
investigations.notice: A lower-bound failure rules a path out; a lower-bound pass does not validate the real path.

investigations.title: Fit before speed
investigations.question: Does the proposed resource change repair capacity, movement, or arithmetic?
investigations.interaction: Keep the task fixed and test resource-specific interventions; distinguish SRAM from flash on tiny endpoints and resident working state elsewhere.
investigations.notice: A configuration that does not fit has no executable timing claim. More arithmetic cannot supply missing capacity.

investigations.title: Keep useful operation
investigations.question: Does the energy-saving policy still provide the required service?
investigations.interaction: Change a supported operating policy or mission allowance while displaying useful service, mission energy, and sustained power separately. For powered endpoints, use node operating allowances rather than inventing a battery.
investigations.notice: Turning the system off saves energy but can fail the mission; extra energy does not raise a sustained-power ceiling.

investigations.title: Make the placement decision
investigations.question: Which paths survive a changed requirement, and what new obligations do survivors create?
investigations.interaction: Show the inherited saved conditions, vary one connection or data-permission requirement, then explicitly select placement or hold and a rejected alternative.
investigations.notice: Filtered or partitioned paths add local work, task-retention evidence, version dependencies, and data-handling obligations.

chapters.turning_point: The processor upgrade can lose to a smaller payload, or every tested path can fail. A hold supported by the gates is a useful decision.
chapters.dossier_entry: Placement record: saved operating case, survivors and exclusions, conditional placement or hold, partition dependencies, unresolved target measurements and complete-cost boundary.
chapters.transition: Placement creates dependencies. The next lab asks what must change when a late requirement invalidates part of the plan.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter explains why deployment categories face different locality and resource constraints. In the lab, test the consequences of moving or partitioning work. Recommend a conditional placement or hold and name the target evidence still required.

chapters.headline: A late requirement makes earlier work conditional
chapters.opening: A requirement changes after the team has already collected data, trained a candidate, and prepared a package. The team must decide what can be preserved and what must be repaired. Finding a defect is only the beginning of that decision.
chapters.previous: Bring the placement assumptions and candidate requirements. A supplied checkpoint identifies the dataset, transforms, model, package, and evidence dependencies if prior records are unavailable.
chapters.goal: Trace a requirement through the lifecycle and plan a justified repair, retest, and return path.

investigations.title: Make the requirement travel
investigations.question: Which artifacts depend on the changed requirement?
investigations.interaction: Mark revise/preserve choices on a dependency graph, then inspect the affected artifact versions and unsupported claims.
investigations.notice: Neither rebuilding everything nor changing packaging alone is a general solution.

investigations.title: Choose the checking point
investigations.question: When does an earlier target check buy more useful development?
investigations.interaction: Move discovery of the same defect between development stages while preserving repair tasks and resource assumptions.
investigations.notice: Early checking costs time but can avoid downstream rework; effort and elapsed schedule are different quantities.

investigations.title: Repair and retest
investigations.question: Do comprehensive checks make the candidate ready?
investigations.interaction: Select an evidence bundle, perform a supported repair, and rerun the affected gate on the identified package.
investigations.notice: Detected failure, repaired-but-unverified, missing evidence, and passing evidence are distinct states.

investigations.title: Route the first field signal
investigations.question: What can the team infer before representative outcomes arrive?
investigations.interaction: Replay a fixed signal/label timeline and choose the owner and next evidence request.
investigations.notice: Referral-only outcomes or changed inputs cannot establish population-wide damage or a successful repair.

chapters.turning_point: The combined checks find the seeded defect but do not fix it. Release still requires a compatible repair and new evidence.
chapters.dossier_entry: Lifecycle map: requirements and artifact dependencies, preserved and revised identities, checking/repair schedule, release obligations, and the owner of the next investigation.
chapters.transition: The team needs a dependable input contract before it can reason about a learned program. Data engineering now turns the raw collection into traceable training and evaluation evidence.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter follows concrete artifacts around the ML lifecycle. In the lab, change a requirement, trace the rework, and distinguish inspection from repair and retest. Hand off the affected data and artifact contracts.

chapters.headline: Make the evidence trustworthy and deliverable
chapters.opening: The collection is growing, but the team cannot yet agree what the labels mean, which examples are independent, or whether training and deployment see the same transformation. Meanwhile, the accelerator waits for input. The next problem is the data system.
chapters.previous: Bring the task definition, lifecycle dependencies, and a frozen raw-record pool. Keep raw observations separate from derived data and evaluation claims.
chapters.goal: Create a versioned data contract that supports independent evaluation and a functioning input path.

investigations.title: Decide what correct means
investigations.question: How should a limited review budget be spent?
investigations.interaction: Allocate annotation or targeted adjudication on the same record pool; inspect disagreement and compare a changed rubric without rewriting predictions.
investigations.notice: Agreement is not automatically truth, and broader annotation competes with resolving consequential ambiguity.

investigations.title: Protect independent evidence
investigations.question: Does a favorable score survive a valid split and fitted-state boundary?
investigations.interaction: Compare record and entity/session splits, then fit-on-train versus fit-before-split; replay serving with frozen versus refitted state.
investigations.notice: Shared entities and preprocessing leakage can inflate evidence without improving behavior.

investigations.title: Feed the consumer
investigations.question: Which pipeline intervention actually raises delivered input?
investigations.interaction: Compare representation, read/decode/transform supply, and consumer demand; improve the binding stage while holding data semantics fixed.
investigations.notice: Smaller files can add decode work. A faster producer is wasted once the consumer becomes limiting.

investigations.title: Diagnose the changed batch
investigations.question: Is this a producer defect, a benign shift, or an unresolved outcome question?
investigations.interaction: Replay a semantic contract violation, repair it, and trace affected descendants; compare a counterexample where an alert alone establishes no harm.
investigations.notice: Schema validity does not establish semantic correctness; detection has validation and quarantine costs.

chapters.turning_point: The clean-looking score can collapse after the split is repaired, and denser compression can leave the accelerator waiting longer.
chapters.dossier_entry: Data manifest: raw and derived identities, label rubric, split groups, fitted preprocessing state, producer checks, lineage, and delivered pipeline capacity.
chapters.transition: The team now has a defensible input contract. It can inspect what the neural computation actually requires before choosing more elaborate structures.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter connects labels, splits, transformations, lineage, and input delivery. In the lab, repair an evidence boundary and a data-path bottleneck. Preserve the resulting data manifest for later model comparisons.

chapters.headline: Open the model and inspect its state
chapters.opening: A teammate proposes a wider or deeper model. Before making a quality claim, the team needs to understand the computation and the state that the proposal creates. A package that fits for inference may still be impossible to train on the development host.
chapters.previous: Bring the data shape, preprocessing contract, deployment allowance, and separate development-host boundary. This is a computation investigation, not a claim that larger models learn better.
chapters.goal: Explain how topology, gradient dependencies, phase, and batching change work, movement, and live state.

investigations.title: Change topology
investigations.question: Does width or depth change every part of the computation in the same way?
investigations.interaction: Inspect layer-level work and parameter/activation allocations after a supported topology change; contrast linear composition with a required nonlinear mapping.
investigations.notice: Parameter count alone neither explains expressivity nor captures every computation cost.

investigations.title: Keep what differentiation needs
investigations.question: Can the weight gradient be computed after its required forward value is discarded?
investigations.interaction: Step through a small dependency graph and remove or restore the values needed by the derivative.
investigations.notice: Missing state is not a zero gradient. The backward pass has a concrete dependency contract.

investigations.title: Separate training and inference
investigations.question: Does endpoint inference fit imply host training fit?
investigations.interaction: Compare phase-specific allocations for the same model and vary the batch without silently changing optimizer or numerical format.
investigations.notice: Weights, saved activations, gradients, and optimizer state scale differently.

investigations.title: Trade reuse for live state
investigations.question: Can batching improve reuse and still make the design infeasible?
investigations.interaction: Grow a supported batch and inspect weight traffic per useful example beside activation memory and capacity.
investigations.notice: Better arithmetic intensity is valuable only inside a legal state budget; this does not yet design a serving scheduler.

chapters.turning_point: A configuration can use the machine more efficiently per example while exceeding the live-state budget. The resource-efficient direction is not automatically a feasible configuration.
chapters.dossier_entry: Computation ledger: shapes, layer work, phase-specific state, required gradient dependencies, and a justified batch/state envelope.
chapters.transition: The next question is structural: which architecture preserves the information the task needs, and which new resource pressures does it create?
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter exposes neural work and state. In the lab, change topology, trace a gradient dependency, and compare training and inference allocations. Explain a reuse improvement that fails a capacity requirement.

chapters.headline: Choose structure for the task, not the label
chapters.opening: A new requirement exposes a weakness in the current model: a condition is missed, a category is absent, or a new item lacks history. The team considers a more sophisticated architecture. Its name alone says nothing about task suitability or deployability.
chapters.previous: Bring the task evidence, data contract, and computation ledger. Architecture candidates must share the declared evaluation task; a language reference remains a separately identified transfer experiment.
chapters.goal: Choose a task-supported architecture while explaining its information assumptions and dominant resource regime.

investigations.title: Keep the right information
investigations.question: Which invariance or structural bias helps this task, and which information would it discard?
investigations.interaction: Compare supplied task-matched candidates and transformations under the stated output requirement.
investigations.notice: A property useful for presence classification may be harmful when location or ordering matters.

investigations.title: Map structure to resources
investigations.question: Would arithmetic, bandwidth, or capacity be the useful intervention?
investigations.interaction: Trace dense work, shared/local operations, or embedding lookup using controlled candidate cases.
investigations.notice: Architectural structure changes movement and state as well as arithmetic.

investigations.title: Stress input and phase
investigations.question: Does longer history have the same consequence during known-input processing and generation?
investigations.interaction: Use a named sequence reference. At fixed supported history, compare materialized and unmaterialized attention scores; inspect retained state alongside unchanged dense score arithmetic, then compare prefill with decode. Retain the distinction between the native mission and the reference task.
investigations.notice: Avoiding a materialized score matrix changes storage, not the quadratic dense score work. History, retained state, and generation phases have different costs. These observations do not make the ring or car a language service.

investigations.title: Test capacity without confusing work
investigations.question: Does a larger category or embedding vocabulary necessarily mean proportionally more work per request?
investigations.interaction: Vary a supported table/vocabulary envelope while holding requested rows fixed; compare task evidence separately.
investigations.notice: Capacity can grow while per-request access remains similar; adding IDs cannot create evidence for an unseen item.

chapters.turning_point: The strongest-looking architecture can remove information the task needs or create a capacity problem that more arithmetic cannot repair.
chapters.dossier_entry: Architecture decision: task-matched candidate identity, required invariances/information, supported input and state envelope, supplied outcome evidence, and explicit reference-study limits.
chapters.transition: The architecture is still a computation specification. The framework lab asks which runtime can actually execute it and whether setup costs earn their keep.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter relates architectural structure to information and resource use. In the lab, compare task-supported candidates, investigate their binding regimes, and keep reference-task conclusions separate from project evidence.

chapters.headline: Make the graph executable
chapters.opening: The candidate works in an exploratory environment, but deployment introduces graph breaks, repeated dispatch, compilation costs, and unsupported operators. The team needs an execution plan rather than a preference for a framework brand.
chapters.previous: Bring the required graph, input signatures, computation dependencies, development/deployment locations, and architecture candidate.
chapters.goal: Choose an execution plan whose visibility, setup costs, backward state, and target support match the work.

investigations.title: Expose the graph
investigations.question: What changes when the same work is visible as a region rather than many calls?
investigations.interaction: Compare eager dispatch, captured regions, and supported fusion while separating submission overhead from changed memory traffic.
investigations.notice: Fewer launches and fewer intermediate transfers are different mechanisms; neither proves that arithmetic disappeared.

investigations.title: Pay for compilation
investigations.question: Will steady-state savings repay setup before the graph changes again?
investigations.interaction: Vary the supported reuse horizon and signature churn for the same graph.
investigations.notice: A compiled plan can be faster per invocation and slower over the actual experiment or deployment horizon.

investigations.title: Automate the backward contract
investigations.question: What must the runtime retain or regenerate for differentiation?
investigations.interaction: Reuse the Lab 05 graph and inspect saved-value policies, reverse traversal, and recomputation consequences on the development host.
investigations.notice: Automatic differentiation manages dependencies; it does not remove them.

investigations.title: Reach the target
investigations.question: Does every required operation have an executable path?
investigations.interaction: Compare native support, explicit partition/fallback, and rejected export on the same graph and shapes.
investigations.notice: Fallback has boundaries and costs. Deleting required preprocessing or postprocessing is a changed task, not a successful export.

chapters.turning_point: The fastest steady-state plan can lose when signatures change, or fail to execute a required operator on the target.
chapters.dossier_entry: Execution contract: graph and signatures, runtime/export identity, location, setup and repeated-work costs, reuse condition, required backward state, and unsupported paths.
chapters.transition: An executable graph does not establish a successful trained model. The next lab chooses a host training recipe and asks when it reaches useful quality.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter explains execution visibility, compilation, differentiation, and target support. In the lab, choose a plan for the actual reuse horizon and verify the required graph can execute. Preserve its runtime and shape contract.

chapters.headline: Train to a target, not to a busy GPU
chapters.opening: The candidate exhausts the development-host memory reservation. A faster numerical recipe is proposed, but its progress is uncertain. The team needs a recipe that fits and reaches the same declared target, rather than the most impressive utilization display.
chapters.previous: Bring the versioned data, architecture, graph/runtime contract, target evidence requirement, and a separately identified development host.
chapters.goal: Choose or reject a training recipe using state fit, effective batch, numerical progress, and a cause-specific bottleneck diagnosis.

investigations.title: Inventory training state
investigations.question: Which allocations disappear when adaptation scope is reduced?
investigations.interaction: Compare supported full and restricted adaptation with weights, gradients, optimizer state, and activations shown separately.
investigations.notice: Freezing parameters need not remove all forward state or backward dependencies.

investigations.title: Recover a nonfitting run
investigations.question: Can accumulation or recomputation preserve the target while fitting?
investigations.interaction: Compare supported resident, micro-batch/accumulated, and checkpointed configurations at the same effective batch where appropriate.
investigations.notice: Lower memory has execution costs; equivalence requires an explicit recipe rather than a familiar batch label.

investigations.title: Judge useful progress
investigations.question: Can faster arithmetic take longer to reach the target or fail to reach it?
investigations.interaction: Reveal matched observed progress for supported numerical recipes; retain failed and unavailable target outcomes.
investigations.notice: Step time and time to acceptable quality are different outcomes; never synthesize accuracy from a speed slider.

investigations.title: Diagnose before spending
investigations.question: Which intervention addresses the revealed critical stage?
investigations.interaction: Inspect partially revealed profiles, test an ineffective improvement, then compare a supported cause-specific repair.
investigations.notice: Busy accelerators do not prove useful learning, and input preparation is not always the bottleneck.

chapters.turning_point: The fast recipe can fail the quality target, while the low-memory recipe can fit but miss the development window.
chapters.dossier_entry: Training record: exact data/model/runtime identities, adaptation and numerical recipe, fit evidence, observed target progress or failure, and the next validation obligation.
chapters.transition: Training has exposed the cost of repeatedly processing the collection. The next lab asks which examples earn that work and whether selecting them truly saves time.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter links training state, execution, numerical behavior, and time to quality. In the lab, recover a nonfitting run and judge matched progress. Training occurs on the development host; endpoint qualification remains a separate obligation.

chapters.headline: Make fewer examples earn their cost
chapters.opening: The archive contains many easy repetitions and too few consequential cases. A smaller selected pool is proposed to accelerate training. The team must determine whether it preserves useful coverage, repays preparation, and changes the actual input path.
chapters.previous: Bring the frozen pool, label/split contract, host training recipe, and common target-quality requirement. A new subset is a new data identity and requires applicable training evidence.
chapters.goal: Choose a selected pool or retain the full pool using learning value, coverage, complete preparation cost, and realized delivery.

investigations.title: Buy useful learning
investigations.question: Should the next fixed work allocation repeat data, add novel cases, or change model/data balance?
investigations.interaction: Choose among supported allocation pilots and reveal work-matched learning observations.
investigations.notice: Fewer examples or a high early gain ratio does not establish reaching the final target.

investigations.title: Spend the coverage budget
investigations.question: Which high-scoring examples must be displaced to preserve required conditions?
investigations.interaction: Allocate a finite subset under justified class/slice floors and inspect an infeasible budget or deficient eligible pool.
investigations.notice: Coverage has an opportunity cost; meeting counts alone does not establish adequate outcomes.

investigations.title: Charge selection honestly
investigations.question: Does saved training work repay scoring, preparation, and refresh?
investigations.interaction: Compare complete campaign accounting for supported scorer preparation and reuse horizons at matched accepted quality.
investigations.notice: A ranking is not free; a changed task may invalidate its reuse.

investigations.title: Realize the saving
investigations.question: Do fewer selected records mean fewer reads or a faster critical path?
investigations.interaction: Keep selected identities fixed and compare stream/discard, scattered reads, and materialized subsets.
investigations.notice: Repacking adds work and storage. Arithmetic savings can remain unrealized when the loader still scans the original archive.

chapters.turning_point: The best-scored subset can violate coverage, and the acceptable subset can lose once selection and loading costs are charged.
chapters.dossier_entry: Data-policy record: selected identities or full-pool decision, coverage and quality evidence, scorer/refresh provenance, materialization choice, and complete cost boundary.
chapters.transition: Changing the training pool reopens the training evidence. Once a compatible candidate exists, the team must turn it into an executable deployment artifact.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter asks when selection improves learning per unit of work. In the lab, choose a pool under coverage obligations, charge its preparation, and test whether the input path realizes the saving. Retaining the full pool is a valid result.

chapters.headline: The checkpoint is not the deployed artifact
chapters.opening: A promising checkpoint is converted for the endpoint and fails a package or live-state allowance. A teammate proposes fewer bits or more zeros. The team must test the exact executable artifact rather than multiply attractive compression ratios.
chapters.previous: Bring a compatible trained candidate, calibration/evaluation identities, endpoint memory tiers, and runtime support. If Lab 09 changed the data, carry new compatible training evidence or use a labeled supplied checkpoint.
chapters.goal: Choose a supported deployment artifact on a quality/resource frontier, or hold conversion when evidence is missing.

investigations.title: Locate the failing allocation
investigations.question: Does a smaller stored package repair the live-memory failure?
investigations.interaction: Change a supported representation while retaining separate weight storage, working state, buffers, and runtime allocations.
investigations.notice: Storage savings may leave the binding live-state allocation untouched.

investigations.title: Evaluate the numerical artifact
investigations.question: Does additional preparation rescue a narrower representation?
investigations.interaction: Compare supported post-training and training-aware candidates on matched calibration and held-out cases.
investigations.notice: Quality recovery is supplied evidence, not guaranteed by the technique name; preparation has a cost.

investigations.title: Follow representation into execution
investigations.question: Do zeros or fewer bits remove executed work on this runtime?
investigations.interaction: Compare masked, indexed, structurally smaller, and supported precision paths with metadata and conversion included.
investigations.notice: Payload reduction, traffic reduction, and faster kernels are different claims.

investigations.title: Test the composition
investigations.question: Does combining useful transformations still produce a supported candidate?
investigations.interaction: Compare exact ordered artifacts against single transformations, preserving missing outcome evidence and unsupported paths.
investigations.notice: Independent ratios do not certify a composite artifact; fixed work remains and transformation order can matter.

chapters.turning_point: The smallest file can fail live memory, execute through a dense path, or lose required task behavior.
chapters.dossier_entry: Deployment bundle: exact task-specific model, transforms, associated state and representation, calibration and quality evidence, runtime identity, resource gates, rejected artifact, and open obligations.
chapters.transition: The chosen representation constrains executable hardware mappings. The next lab tests the machine and dataflow without dropping the complete application path.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter distinguishes compressed representations from useful executable artifacts. In the lab, test quality, live state, runtime support, and actual combinations. Hand off one identified bundle rather than a collection of independent ratios.

chapters.headline: A faster kernel must survive the whole path
chapters.opening: The target advertises more arithmetic throughput, but the complete response barely improves. The team must identify the relevant interface, map legal work, and count movement before recommending a machine or schedule.
chapters.previous: Bring the exact deployment bundle, supported operations, data shapes, and complete-path decomposition. Capacity failures remain failures, not invented spill-time estimates.
chapters.goal: Choose a legal mapping and resource intervention with counted traffic and an explained application-level consequence.

investigations.title: Move the useful ceiling
investigations.question: Which resource improvement changes this workload bound?
investigations.interaction: Compare arithmetic, bandwidth, and supported reuse interventions on the relevant roofline.
investigations.notice: The limiting regime belongs to a workload and interface, not permanently to a model family.

investigations.title: Choose what stays
investigations.question: Which operand should remain resident?
investigations.interaction: Step through supported stationary schedules and count weight, activation, and partial-sum movement with its energy consequences.
investigations.notice: Avoiding one category of traffic can increase another.

investigations.title: Find a legal tile
investigations.question: Does the largest tile fit and use the machine effectively?
investigations.interaction: Grow a supported tile, cross live-buffer/accumulator capacity, and compare an off-grid shape or aligned alternative.
investigations.notice: Reuse competes with state, alignment, and fringe work; illegal configurations have no valid runtime.

investigations.title: Return to the application
investigations.question: How much of the end-to-end path did the improvement actually change?
investigations.interaction: Carry the selected legal intervention through decode, host work, transfers, kernel, and postprocessing; preserve fallbacks.
investigations.notice: An isolated kernel gain is capped by untouched work and may move the bottleneck elsewhere.

chapters.turning_point: More peak arithmetic can do little, while a modest legal movement reduction can help. Either can become insignificant outside the kernel.
chapters.dossier_entry: Mapping record: target/runtime assumptions, legal tile or dataflow, counted traffic, resource regime, full-path consequence, and remaining profiling evidence.
chapters.transition: The team now has a performance argument. Benchmarking asks whether the evidence actually supports the proposed claim under relevant conditions.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter connects hardware ceilings, dataflow, tiling, and movement. In the lab, select a legal intervention and carry it through the complete path. Explain which resource changed and which application limit remained.

chapters.headline: Earn the right to make a performance claim
chapters.opening: A warm, favorable measurement is placed in the release presentation. It may be correct for its narrow timer boundary and still be misleading about everyday behavior. The team needs a reproducible claim with matched artifacts, conditions, populations, and uncertainty.
chapters.previous: Bring the exact bundle, mapping, input/data identities, intended workload, quality obligation, and proposed complete-path claim.
chapters.goal: Decide which performance and behavioral claims are supported, contradicted, or still unresolved.

investigations.title: Match the boundary
investigations.question: Do the two favorable numbers measure the same work?
investigations.interaction: Choose the claim, expose a protocol mismatch, repair timer endpoints or included stages, and rerun the supported comparison.
investigations.notice: Matching a model name does not match a measurement protocol.

investigations.title: Spend the measurement budget
investigations.question: Where do independent repeats buy evidence?
investigations.interaction: Allocate a fixed budget between requests and independent paired runs, retaining within-run and between-run variation.
investigations.notice: More correlated requests need not resolve uncertainty; detectable improvement and useful improvement differ.

investigations.title: Challenge representativeness
investigations.question: Does the result survive the relevant sustained or local condition?
investigations.interaction: Replay supported workload/condition traces and inspect tails, deadline misses, or complete-window energy beside the headline.
investigations.notice: An idle, warm, or short run supports only the corresponding operating envelope.

investigations.title: Audit the behavior claim
investigations.question: Can equal aggregate quality hide consequential differences?
investigations.interaction: Lock quality gates, reveal paired slices and calibration, and test a supported repair without inventing missing coverage.
investigations.notice: Calibration can change while classifications remain fixed. Untested populations remain untested.

chapters.turning_point: The headline speedup can become unresolved after matching protocols, or fail in the conditions the project actually serves.
chapters.dossier_entry: Benchmark claim card: artifact and protocol identities, timer boundary, workload/population, conditions, uncertainty, quality gates, supported claim, and untested scope.
chapters.transition: A credible benchmark does not establish service under arrivals. The next lab introduces waiting, admission, live state, and the cost of keeping responses timely.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter teaches what a benchmark can support. In the lab, repair a comparison, allocate independent evidence, and challenge operating conditions and behavioral coverage. Submit a bounded claim rather than the most favorable number.

chapters.headline: Serve useful work when demand arrives
chapters.opening: Demand becomes bursty. The average execution time still looks good while useful work waits, arrives late, or is silently dropped. The team must choose a service policy and count what it sacrifices.
chapters.previous: Bring the benchmarked bundle, complete-path timing, live-state budget, and declared useful-service requirement. Endpoint freshness and behavioral quality remain distinct obligations.
chapters.goal: Choose a serving policy with an explicit demand envelope, waiting behavior, state fit, and lost-service accounting.

investigations.title: Budget the whole service
investigations.question: Which stage reaches the user, and which local improvement survives?
investigations.interaction: Compare supported host/model interventions on the same full service path.
investigations.notice: A forward pass is only part of the service, and moving work can add transfer or preparation.

investigations.title: Keep headroom honestly
investigations.question: Does improved tail latency come from better service or refusing more work?
investigations.interaction: Replay the same arrivals while changing admission or a supported capacity policy; inspect backlog and lost work beside latency.
investigations.notice: A favorable percentile with a changed accepted-work denominator is an incomplete claim.

investigations.title: Form work deliberately
investigations.question: Does waiting for a batch actually save execution?
investigations.interaction: Compare immediate and supported batch dispatch on identical traces; separate formation delay, realized groups, executed work, and deadline outcomes.
investigations.notice: A longer batching window adds waiting even when it produces no batching benefit.

investigations.title: Fit live work
investigations.question: Do the weights fitting imply the service can run its live workload?
investigations.interaction: Cross and recover native buffer/concurrency capacity; keep any generative phase/KV comparison a separately named reference.
investigations.notice: Model residency, per-request state, and native task requirements are different. A ranking embedding table is not a KV cache.

chapters.turning_point: The policy with the best displayed latency can have rejected the most useful work, and the largest batch can add delay without reducing execution.
chapters.dossier_entry: Service policy: exact bundle, supported arrival/demand envelope, dispatch/admission choice, live-state reservation, tails and lost-service counts, freshness obligation, and reversal trigger.
chapters.transition: The service is now a changing operational system. The next lab asks whether an update can be diagnosed, deployed, and recovered without losing its evidence contract.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter connects execution to arrivals, waiting, state, and useful service. In the lab, compare policies on identical demand and count deferred or rejected work. Retain the policy only within its supported operating envelope.

chapters.headline: An update breaks the contract without crashing
chapters.opening: The process is healthy after an update, but outputs change on paired inputs. Outcome labels will arrive later. The team must decide what the early signal means, identify what actually ran, and recover a compatible service.
chapters.previous: Bring the deployed bundle, preprocessing/feature identities, service envelope, benchmark protocol, and owners of its behavioral and operational obligations.
chapters.goal: Create an evidence-based incident response with replayable lineage, feasible rollout, and tested recovery.

investigations.title: Observe without assuming
investigations.question: What can the team infer now, before delayed outcomes mature?
investigations.interaction: Choose a monitor, replay early and late evidence windows, and compare alert sensitivity with confirmation and response cost.
investigations.notice: An alert is a request for investigation, not proof of damage or a justified retraining action.

investigations.title: Replay what ran
investigations.question: Does distributional similarity or a version label establish parity?
investigations.interaction: Compare request-keyed transformed values and immutable release identities; repair a supplied mismatch while preserving the original inputs.
investigations.notice: Aggregate distributions can hide swapped values; replay needs artifacts, fitted state, and provenance.

investigations.title: Reserve a safe transition
investigations.question: Does a small exposure share imply a small resident-memory cost?
investigations.interaction: Change canary exposure, inspect complete candidate/baseline reservations, and choose a feasible staged or held rollout.
investigations.notice: Exposure, evidence strength, copy residency, and simultaneous execution are separate quantities.

investigations.title: Recover the cause
investigations.question: Does reverting weights restore the system?
investigations.interaction: Test an inadequate rollback, then recover the compatible transform/model/runtime/state bundle; contrast a population shift that rollback cannot repair.
investigations.notice: Containment is not verified recovery, and the right response depends on the cause.

chapters.turning_point: The tiny canary can fail memory, and the model rollback can leave the incompatible preprocessing or state that caused the incident.
chapters.dossier_entry: Operations record: incident and owner, monitoring/evidence maturity, exact release lineage, feasible rollout reservation, tested recovery, and remaining claims.
chapters.transition: The team can operate the mechanism. It still needs to justify whose outcomes matter, what feedback hides, and which costs and restrictions govern use.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter links monitoring, versioned artifacts, rollout, and recovery. In the lab, investigate a healthy-looking incident and test a compatible response. Do not substitute an alert or weight rollback for verified recovery.

chapters.headline: Useful for whom, under which obligations?
chapters.opening: The system meets attractive aggregate metrics. Some affected groups have weak evidence, and the feedback comes mainly from the cases the system chose to show or users chose to correct. The team must decide which claims and uses it can defend.
chapters.previous: Bring the intended use, held-out outcomes and their sampling limits, service policy, incident evidence, and declared lifecycle accounting boundary. Responsibility obligations existed earlier; this lab evaluates them together.
chapters.goal: Recommend release, restricted use, baseline retention, mitigation, or hold using justified obligations and observed consequences.

investigations.title: Choose what must pass
investigations.question: Does the proxy represent the intended benefit for the affected population?
investigations.interaction: State the goal and obligation before revealing subgroup and independent outcome evidence.
investigations.notice: Healthy infrastructure and aggregate accuracy do not establish the intended outcome; sparse evidence is not a passing group.

investigations.title: Pay for mitigation
investigations.question: Which supported intervention satisfies the obligation, and what does it cost?
investigations.interaction: Compare matched candidates with separate error consequences, quality/resource gates, and supported mitigation outcomes.
investigations.notice: There is no universal fairness-versus-accuracy slider or scalar score that resolves every obligation.

investigations.title: Inspect the feedback loop
investigations.question: What remains invisible because of what the system chose to observe?
investigations.interaction: Compare observation/audit policies, reveal supplied outcomes, and test a cause-specific response to selective or exposure-conditioned labels.
investigations.notice: The observed trend may not identify the population effect; automation can reinforce a blind spot.

investigations.title: Count the whole decision
investigations.question: Is the cheaper or faster option better under equal useful service?
investigations.interaction: Compare supported lifecycle alternatives with separate dollars, energy, emissions, and preparation/operation boundaries.
investigations.notice: A subsystem saving is not a whole-system claim. Declared exclusions and supported service govern the comparison.

chapters.turning_point: The appealing metric can improve while an independent outcome or justified group obligation fails. The best response may be restricted scope or a hold.
chapters.dossier_entry: Responsibility case: intended use and exclusions, affected populations, governing outcome obligations, evidence sufficiency, mitigation/audit policy, lifecycle boundary, and unresolved gates.
chapters.transition: The final review now needs one coherent argument across behavior, resources, service, operations, and responsibility. It cannot assemble a release from incompatible green results.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The chapter examines intended outcomes, affected populations, feedback, and lifecycle costs. In the lab, challenge a favorable aggregate result and compare supported responses. Defend the permitted scope of use and the evidence still missing.

chapters.headline: Defend one coherent deployment decision
chapters.opening: The release meeting begins. The dossier contains excellent individual results, but they came from different data versions, packages, populations, and operating conditions. Your task is to decide what the exact proposed system can demonstrate now.
chapters.previous: Bring compatible records from earlier labs, with explicit identities and limits. A labeled supplied dossier is available for students joining here; missing history is not silently fabricated.
chapters.goal: Integrate earlier concepts into a release, restriction, baseline, fallback, or hold decision without inventing a new score.

investigations.title: Audit the supporting story
investigations.question: Do these earlier passes refer to the same proposed system?
investigations.interaction: Inspect purported supporting records and replay or reject links by requirement, data, artifact, runtime, protocol, population, and operating identity.
investigations.notice: Completion counts and a shared project name do not establish compatibility.

investigations.title: Carry one improvement through
investigations.question: Does the selected alternative preserve its benefit on the complete path?
investigations.interaction: Reuse a supported candidate comparison and inspect joint resource, behavioral, and service consequences.
investigations.notice: Local wins do not compose automatically; rejected alternatives must be compared under the same contract.

investigations.title: Find the recommendation boundary
investigations.question: What changed requirement would reverse the decision?
investigations.interaction: Tighten a supported allowance or demand condition for the same candidate and test recovery, restricted scope, or hold.
investigations.notice: A new policy limit changes acceptability, not the original measured consumption.

investigations.title: Respond to change
investigations.question: Which claim breaks, and which response addresses that cause?
investigations.interaction: Apply a supported path or population change, identify expired evidence, and test a justified response using familiar instruments.
investigations.notice: Physical feasibility and behavioral validity can expire separately. Rollback is not a universal answer.

chapters.turning_point: A complete notebook history can still support only a hold. A smaller, compatible body of evidence can support a narrower but defensible deployment claim.
chapters.dossier_entry: Final deployment dossier and discussion: exact proposed system, supported use and demand, chosen/rejected options, compatible evidence references, unresolved obligations, owner, reversal trigger, and next decisive test.
chapters.transition: The series ends with a bounded engineering decision, not a victory screen. Students can return to the earliest affected artifact when the next condition changes.
chapters.qmd_bridge: The conclusion integrates the volume rather than introducing a new mechanism. In the lab, audit the dossier, challenge the recommendation, and defend one coherent decision. A well-supported hold completes the investigation.
